questions.explanation: The contrast study shows an irregular annular stricture (apple-core lesion) typical of colorectal carcinoma rather than the smooth coiled-spring appearance of intussusception or the beak-like taper of volvulus.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaportalvenousgas.png ]
questions.explanation: The tiny branching gas foci extend to the peripheral 2 cm of the liver, characteristic of portal venous gas; pneumobilia by contrast is centrally distributed near the porta hepatis.

questions.text: Which is not a typical finding in acute cholecystitis on ultrasound?
questions.explanation: Acute cholecystitis classically shows a thickened (>3 mm), edematous gallbladder wall; a thin, normal wall argues against the diagnosis.

questions.text: Which is Not a typical finding in pancreatitis ?
questions.explanation: Acute pancreatitis causes an enlarged, edematous gland with irregular borders, not a small pancreas; the other options are recognized features/complications.

questions.text: Wrong about hiatal hernia?
options: Rolling (paraesophageal) hernias carry a risk of gastric volvulus
Paraesophageal hernia moves the esophagogastric junction 2 cm above the diaphragm
Sliding hernias are associated with gastroesophageal reflux
Sliding type is the most common
originalOptions: Rolling (paraesophageal) hernias carry a risk of gastric volvulus
Paraesophageal hernia moves the esophagogastric junction 2 cm above the diaphragm
Sliding hernias are associated with gastroesophageal reflux
Sliding type is the most common
questions.correctAnswer: B) Paraesophageal hernia moves the esophagogastric junction 2 cm above the diaphragm
questions.correctAnswerText: Paraesophageal hernia moves the esophagogastric junction 2 cm above the diaphragm
questions.explanation: Upward displacement of the gastroesophageal junction (>2 cm above the hiatus) defines a sliding hiatal hernia, not a paraesophageal one, in which the GEJ stays in normal position while the fundus herniates.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a typical radiological feature of achalasia?
options: Bird-beak appearance at the gastroesophageal junction
Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea
originalOptions: Bird-beak appearance at the gastroesophageal junction
Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea
questions.explanation: Achalasia causes mediastinal widening (not narrowing) from the dilated, fluid-filled esophagus, so calling it "mediastinal narrowing" as a listed feature is incorrect — but among the options here, the true described finding is widening, and identifying "narrowing" as false is the tested trap; the correct fact is mediastinal widening occurs, making a statement of narrowing the false one.

questions.text: Best imaging modality for detecting air under the diaphragm:
questions.explanation: An erect chest film taken in expiration maximizes sensitivity for detecting small amounts of subdiaphragmatic free air, more so than a supine film which cannot show air-fluid levels or subdiaphragmatic air.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycpleuraleffusion.png ]
questions.explanation: Homogeneous opacity with a meniscus sign and blunted costophrenic angle indicates pleural effusion. Pneumonia shows air bronchograms without a meniscus, and pneumothorax is radiolucent.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT seen in heart failure on chest radiography?
questions.explanation: Heart failure typically causes cardiomegaly (cardiothoracic ratio >50%), not a small heart. Edema, effusion, cephalization and Kerley B lines are all typical.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycpneumothorax.png ]
questions.explanation: Right-sided pneumothorax with almost complete collapse of the right lung. Mediastinal shift to the left, splayed right ribs and mild right diaphragm depression indicate increased right pleural pressure. A thin visceral pleural line with no lung markings peripheral to it and a lucent pleural space is diagnostic of pneumothorax. Effusion and consolidation produce opacity instead.

questions.text: Which of the following appears radiolucent (translucent) on chest radiograph?
questions.explanation: Air in the pleural space is black (lucent). Effusion, consolidation, collapse and enlarged nodes are all soft-tissue opacities.

questions.text: All of the following regarding lung anatomy are true EXCEPT:
options: The lingula is seen in the right lung
The right lung has an oblique and a horizontal fissure
The left lung has only an oblique fissure
The left lung has an upper and a lower lobe
The right lung has three lobes
originalOptions: The lingula is seen in the right lung
The right lung has an oblique and a horizontal fissure
The left lung has only an oblique fissure
The left lung has an upper and a lower lobe
The right lung has three lobes
questions.correctAnswer: A) The lingula is seen in the right lung
questions.correctAnswerText: The lingula is seen in the right lung
questions.explanation: The lingula is part of the left upper lobe and replaces the middle lobe on the left. The right lung has an upper, middle and lower lobe.

questions.text: Which statement about aortic dissection is WRONG?
options: It results from a tear in the intima
CT angiography is the investigation of choice
Ultrasound is more commonly used than CT for diagnosis
A false lumen forms within the medial layer
originalOptions: It results from a tear in the intima
CT angiography is the investigation of choice
Ultrasound is more commonly used than CT for diagnosis
A false lumen forms within the medial layer
questions.correctAnswer: D) Ultrasound is more commonly used than CT for diagnosis
questions.correctAnswerText: Ultrasound is more commonly used than CT for diagnosis
questions.explanation: CT, especially CTA, is the diagnostic modality of choice for dissection. Ultrasound has a very limited role.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologympcltear.png ]
questions.explanation: The image shows injury to the posterior cruciate ligament complex; ACL and meniscal tears involve distinct anatomic locations and MRI signal patterns.

questions.text: Which of the following is FALSE regarding slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE)?
options: More commonly affects obese adolescent boys
Considered a Salter-Harris type III fracture
Femoral head slips posteriorly and medially relative to the metaphysis
Represents a Salter-Harris type I fracture through the subcapital physis
originalOptions: More commonly affects obese adolescent boys
Considered a Salter-Harris type III fracture
Femoral head slips posteriorly and medially relative to the metaphysis
Represents a Salter-Harris type I fracture through the subcapital physis
questions.correctAnswer: B) Considered a Salter-Harris type III fracture
questions.correctAnswerText: Considered a Salter-Harris type III fracture
questions.explanation: SCFE is a Salter-Harris type I fracture of the subcapital femoral physis due to chronic weight-bearing stress, not type III.

questions.text: Which of the following is WRONG about rickets on radiograph?
options: Vitamin D deficiency is a cause
originalOptions: Vitamin D deficiency is a cause
questions.explanation: Rickets classically shows cupping, splaying, and fraying of the metaphysis from deficient mineralization, not punched-out lytic lesions (a feature of gout or myeloma).

questions.text: Periosteal reaction is seen in all of the following EXCEPT:

questions.text: Which of the following about hyperparathyroidism is WRONG?

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyndiffuseedema.png ]

questions.text: Which is WRONG about this lesion? [img: Radiologynmeningiomawrong.png ]

questions.text: Most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyacolorectalcancer.png ]

questions.text: Which is Not a typical finding in pancreatitis ?

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyapancreatitis.png ]

questions.text: Which of the following is not a typical radiologic feature of appendicitis?

questions.explanation: The bird-beak deformity is the classic sign of achalasia at the gastroesophageal junction, not a recognized sign of bowel ischemia, unlike portal venous gas, thumbprinting, and wall thickening.

questions.text: What of these is not seen in ischemic colitis?
questions.explanation: Pneumobilia reflects biliary gas and is not a feature of ischemic colitis; thumbprinting, segmental wall thickening, and portal venous gas are all recognized ischemic colitis findings.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about chest radiograph technique is FALSE?

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycaorticdissection.png ]

questions.explanation: The aortic root and ascending aorta are affected in about 60% of cases. The arch accounts for only about 10%.

questions.text: What is the best imaging modality for diagnosing acute pulmonary embolism, for example in a patient with acute hypoxia and dyspnea with a normal chest X-ray?
questions.explanation: CTPA (which utilizes intravenous contrast) directly shows filling defects in the pulmonary arteries, and the chest X-ray is often normal. V/Q scan is only an alternative when contrast is contraindicated.

questions.text: All of the following are seen in heart failure EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Heart failure causes pulmonary edema, cardiomegaly, effusions and Kerley B lines. Pneumothorax is not part of it.

questions.text: Which stage of Salter-Harris fracture is shown? [img: Radiologymsalter3harris.png ]
questions.explanation: The fracture plane runs along the growth plate and extends down through the epiphysis into the joint while sparing the metaphysis — the defining pattern of a Salter-Harris type III injury, which carries a poorer prognosis due to epiphyseal/articular involvement.

questions.text: Which is NOT a feature of a simple bone cyst?
questions.explanation: Unicameral (simple) bone cysts are centrally located within the metaphysis of long bones, not peripheral; they are otherwise well-defined, radiolucent, benign lesions with a narrow zone of transition.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT typically involved in non-traumatic fractures of child abuse?
questions.explanation: Parietal bone fractures are low-specificity findings often due to accidental trauma, whereas metaphyseal corner, posterior rib, and scapular fractures are pathognomonic or highly specific for non-accidental injury.

questions.text: What is the name of the labelled carpal bone (Number 6) ? [img: Radiologymanatomycapitate.png ]
questions.explanation: The capitate is the largest carpal bone, centrally located in the distal carpal row, distinguishing it from the hamate (ulnar side), lunate (proximal row), and trapezoid (radial side).

questions.text: Which of the following about hyperparathyroidism is WRONG?
questions.explanation: Sacroiliitis is a feature of seronegative spondyloarthropathies, not hyperparathyroidism, which instead causes osteopenia, floating teeth, and salt-and-pepper skull.

questions.text: Which artery supplies the infarcted territory shown in this image? [img: Radiologynacainfarct.png ]
questions.explanation: The infarct involves the medial frontal lobe, the classic ACA distribution, unlike the lateral hemispheric MCA territory or the occipital PCA territory.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynmeningioma.png ]
questions.explanation: An extra-axial, dural-based, homogeneously enhancing mass is the classic appearance of meningioma, unlike the crescentic/biconvex hemorrhagic collections of subdural/epidural hematoma.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynmultiplesclerosis.png ]

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyndiffuseedema.png ]
questions.explanation: Loss of grey-white differentiation with a "dense cerebellum sign" and sulcal effacement are classic for diffuse cerebral edema.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynepiduralhematomaacute.png ]
questions.explanation: A biconvex, lentiform hyperdense extra-axial collection is the classic CT appearance of acute epidural hematoma, distinct from the crescentic shape of subdural hematoma.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyadiverticulitis.png ]
questions.explanation: The CT shows sigmoid diverticula with adjacent pericolic fat stranding and mild bowel wall thickening, the classic appearance of diverticulitis rather than isolated diverticulosis.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaportalvenousgas.png ]

questions.text: Best imaging modality for detecting air under the diaphragm:
questions.explanation: An erect chest film taken in expiration maximizes sensitivity for detecting small amounts of subdiaphragmatic free air, more so than a supine film which cannot show air-fluid levels or subdiaphragmatic air.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaachalasia.png ]
questions.explanation: The barium swallow shows a dilated esophagus tapering smoothly to a "bird-beak" narrowing at the gastroesophageal junction, the classic finding of achalasia.

questions.text: The "3-6-9 rule" refers to the approximate maximum normal diameter (in cm) of which structures, respectively?

questions.correctAnswerText: Small bowel (3 cm), large bowel (6 cm), cecum (9 cm)
questions.explanation: The 3-6-9 rule gives the approximate upper limits of normal caliber for the small bowel (3 cm), large bowel (6 cm), and cecum (9 cm) — exceeding these thresholds raises concern for bowel dilatation/obstruction.

questions.text: Which imaging modality is considered the gold standard for detecting gallbladder stones?
questions.explanation: Ultrasound is highly sensitive for gallstones, appearing as echogenic foci with posterior acoustic shadowing, and is far more sensitive than plain radiograph (which only shows ~15–20% of stones) or CT (which can miss cholesterol stones).

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic finding of small bowel obstruction, as opposed to large bowel obstruction?
options: Centrally located dilated loops with valvulae conniventes crossing the full width of the lumen
Haustral folds crossing only part of the lumen
Fecal loading within the dilated bowel segment

questions.correctAnswerText: Centrally located dilated loops with valvulae conniventes crossing the full width of the lumen
questions.explanation: Small bowel lies centrally and shows valvulae conniventes that span the entire lumen diameter, distinguishing it from large bowel, which lies peripherally and shows haustral folds crossing only part of the lumen.

questions.text: Simultaneous visualization of gas within the bowel lumen and gas outlining the outer bowel wall (the double-wall/Rigler sign) is a sign of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Gas outlining both the inner (intraluminal) and outer (extraluminal/peritoneal) surfaces of the bowel wall is the Rigler (double-wall) sign, indicating free intraperitoneal air from a perforated viscus.

questions.text: What is the best imaging modality for evaluating suspected appendicitis in an adult?
questions.explanation: CT with IV contrast has the highest sensitivity (94–98%) and specificity (up to 97%) for appendicitis in adults and also identifies alternative causes of abdominal pain; ultrasound is preferred first-line in children and pregnant patients but is more operator-dependent and less sensitive overall.

questions.text: Which chest radiograph projection makes the heart appear normal in size?
questions.explanation: On the PA view the heart is close to the detector, so magnification is minimal (AP views magnify it), and the erect position prevents the diaphragmatic elevation and mediastinal widening that occur in the supine position.

questions.text: Air bronchograms are a characteristic finding in which of the following?
questions.explanation: In consolidation the alveoli are filled while the bronchi remain patent, so air-filled bronchi are outlined within the homogeneous opacity. They are absent in effusion and pneumothorax, and collapse is defined by volume loss rather than air bronchograms.

questions.text: Why does the heart appear magnified on an AP chest radiograph?
options: The scapulae overlie the cardiac shadow
The patient is usually rotated during the examination
The heart is farther from the detector
The beam traverses the patient from posterior to anterior
The lungs are hyperinflated on AP films
originalOptions: The scapulae overlie the cardiac shadow
The patient is usually rotated during the examination
The heart is farther from the detector
The beam traverses the patient from posterior to anterior
The lungs are hyperinflated on AP films
questions.correctAnswer: C) The heart is farther from the detector
questions.correctAnswerText: The heart is farther from the detector
questions.explanation: Magnification is geometric, because in the AP view the heart lies farther from the detector than in the PA view. Rotation and overlying scapulae are drawbacks of AP films but are not the cause of magnification, and a posterior-to-anterior beam describes the PA view.

questions.text: Which of the following typically causes mediastinal shift AWAY from the affected side?
options: Complete obstruction of the main bronchus
originalOptions: Complete obstruction of the main bronchus
questions.explanation: A large effusion exerts mass effect and pushes the mediastinum away from the affected side. Collapse (including complete main bronchus obstruction) pulls the mediastinum toward the affected side, consolidation preserves volume without shift, and a simple pneumothorax causes no shift unless it becomes tension.

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic sign of pleural effusion on an erect frontal chest radiograph?
questions.explanation: Fluid climbs the lateral chest wall, forming a concave-upward meniscus that slopes gently medially, together with blunting of the costophrenic angle. Air bronchogram indicates consolidation, signet ring indicates bronchiectasis, and cephalization and Kerley B lines are features of heart failure.

The line represents the parietal pleura
The mediastinum always shifts away from the affected side
The peripheral space appears denser than the adjacent lung

The peripheral space is radiolucent compared with the adjacent lung

The mediastinum always shifts away from the affected side
The peripheral space appears denser than the adjacent lung
questions.correctAnswer: B) The peripheral space is radiolucent compared with the adjacent lung
questions.correctAnswerText: The peripheral space is radiolucent compared with the adjacent lung
questions.explanation: The line is the visceral pleural edge, and the air-filled pleural space beyond it is lucent and avascular. Shift away from the pneumothorax occurs only in tension pneumothorax.

questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE regarding heart failure on chest radiography?
options: Pleural effusions are not a feature
Cephalization of the pulmonary vessels is seen
Kerley B lines are long lines at the lung apices
The cardiothoracic ratio is typically below 50%
originalOptions: Pleural effusions are not a feature
Cephalization of the pulmonary vessels is seen
Kerley B lines are long lines at the lung apices
The cardiothoracic ratio is typically below 50%
questions.correctAnswer: C) Cephalization of the pulmonary vessels is seen
questions.correctAnswerText: Cephalization of the pulmonary vessels is seen
questions.explanation: Pulmonary venous congestion dilates the upper lobe veins (cephalization). Heart failure causes cardiomegaly (cardiothoracic ratio >50%) and effusions, and Kerley B lines are 1–2 cm peripheral lines at the lung bases, not the apices.

questions.text: A chest radiograph shows a thin visceral pleural line with absent lung markings peripheral to it and no mediastinal shift. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: A visible visceral pleural edge with an avascular lucent space beyond it is diagnostic of pneumothorax, and the absence of mediastinal shift makes it non-tension. Tension pneumothorax shifts the mediastinum away, and effusion, collapse and consolidation all produce opacity.

questions.text: Which of the following is INCORRECT regarding child abuse injuries?
options: Metaphyseal corner fractures are highly specific for abuse
Posterior rib fractures are strongly associated with intentional injury
Epidural hematoma is more specific for abuse than subdural hematoma
Scapular fractures carry a high specificity for physical abuse
originalOptions: Metaphyseal corner fractures are highly specific for abuse
Posterior rib fractures are strongly associated with intentional injury
Epidural hematoma is more specific for abuse than subdural hematoma
Scapular fractures carry a high specificity for physical abuse
questions.correctAnswer: C) Epidural hematoma is more specific for abuse than subdural hematoma
questions.correctAnswerText: Epidural hematoma is more specific for abuse than subdural hematoma
questions.explanation: Subdural hematomas (not epidural) are highly specific and characteristic of non-accidental trauma, while metaphyseal corner, posterior rib, and scapular fractures are well-established indicators of child abuse.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymnonossifyingfibroma.png ]
questions.explanation: A multiloculated lucent metaphyseal lesion with a sclerotic rim, larger than 3 cm and eccentrically placed near the physis, is a non-ossifying fibroma.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymperthesdisease.png ]
questions.explanation: Femoral head deformity and flattening with widening of joint space and blurring of the physeal plate on the left.

questions.text: Which of the following is FALSE regarding ankylosing spondylitis?
options: Interspinous ligament ossification gives a "dagger spine" appearance
originalOptions: Interspinous ligament ossification gives a "dagger spine" appearance
questions.explanation: Ankylosing spondylitis has a male predilection of about 3:1 or more, making "more common in females" the false statement.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a tarsal bone?
questions.explanation: The trapezium is a carpal (wrist) bone; the seven tarsal bones are the talus, calcaneus, navicular, cuboid, and three cuneiforms.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a carpal bone?
questions.explanation: The talus is a tarsal bone of the ankle, not one of the eight carpal bones of the wrist.

questions.text: Which of the following is WRONG (not a feature) regarding gout?
options: Preservation of joint space until late in disease
originalOptions: Preservation of joint space until late in disease
questions.explanation: The dagger spine sign results from interspinous ligament ossification in ankylosing spondylitis, not gout, which instead produces punched-out erosions and tophi.

questions.text: Which of the following is WRONG about osteoarthritis?
questions.explanation: Osteoarthritis characteristically produces asymmetric joint-space narrowing, unlike the symmetric pattern seen in rheumatoid arthritis.

questions.text: All of the following are benign bone lesions EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Osteosarcoma is a malignant bone-forming tumor, while osteochondroma, osteoid osteoma, and non-ossifying fibroma are all benign lesions.

questions.text: Which periosteal reaction pattern is typically associated with a benign process?
questions.explanation: A solid, smooth periosteal reaction reflects a slow-growing process and is typically benign, unlike the aggressive sunburst, onion-skin, or Codman triangle patterns.

questions.text: Which of the following is WRONG (not a feature) of rickets?
options: Rachitic rosary at the costochondral junctions
Subperiosteal resorption of the radial aspect of the 2nd and 3rd middle phalanges
originalOptions: Rachitic rosary at the costochondral junctions
Subperiosteal resorption of the radial aspect of the 2nd and 3rd middle phalanges
questions.correctAnswer: D) Subperiosteal resorption of the radial aspect of the 2nd and 3rd middle phalanges
questions.correctAnswerText: Subperiosteal resorption of the radial aspect of the 2nd and 3rd middle phalanges
questions.explanation: This subperiosteal resorption pattern is a hallmark of hyperparathyroidism, not rickets, which instead shows cupping, splaying, fraying, and rachitic rosary.

questions.text: In this labeled axial CT image, what does structure "3" represent? [img: Radiologyaleftrenalvein.png ]
questions.explanation: In this labeled slice the numbered structures correspond to liver, gallbladder, and left renal vein, consistent with the vein's typical course anterior to the aorta toward the IVC, the characteristic path of the left renal vein (it crosses anterior to the aorta, unlike the renal artery which lies posterior to the vein).
questions.note: 1. Liver || 2. Gallbladder || 3. Left renal vein

questions.text: Not true about achalasia?
options: Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea is seen on the frontal view
originalOptions: Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea is seen on the frontal view
questions.correctAnswer: D) Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea is seen on the frontal view
questions.correctAnswerText: Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea is seen on the frontal view
questions.explanation: Anterior tracheal displacement/bowing from the dilated esophagus is a lateral-view finding, not a frontal-view finding, making this statement false.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about radiologic imaging is incorrect?
options: Female ovarian assessment requires an empty urinary bladder
Ultrasound is effective for evaluating the biliary and urinary systems
Single contrast enema uses only barium without air
Free intraperitoneal air can be seen under the diaphragm on an erect chest X-ray
originalOptions: Female ovarian assessment requires an empty urinary bladder
Ultrasound is effective for evaluating the biliary and urinary systems
Single contrast enema uses only barium without air
Free intraperitoneal air can be seen under the diaphragm on an erect chest X-ray
questions.correctAnswer: A) Female ovarian assessment requires an empty urinary bladder
questions.correctAnswerText: Female ovarian assessment requires an empty urinary bladder
questions.explanation: Transabdominal pelvic/ovarian ultrasound requires a FULL bladder as an acoustic window, not an empty one; the other statements are correct.

questions.text: All are signs of pneumoperitoneum except:
questions.explanation: There is no recognized "single-wall sign" for pneumoperitoneum — the real analogous sign is the double-wall (Rigler) sign, where gas outlines both sides of the bowel wall.

questions.text: Which finding characterizes right middle lobe pneumonia on a frontal chest radiograph?
questions.correctAnswer: A) Obscures the right heart border
questions.explanation: The right middle lobe abuts the right heart border, so consolidation there produces the silhouette sign. Right lower lobe consolidation obscures the hemidiaphragm, and lingular consolidation obscures the left heart border.

questions.text: Which chest radiograph projection makes the heart appear normal in size?
questions.explanation: On the PA view the heart is close to the detector, so magnification is minimal (AP views magnify it), and the erect position prevents the diaphragmatic elevation and mediastinal widening that occur in the supine position.

questions.text: Which of the following is characteristic of post-primary (reactivation) tuberculosis?
options: Ipsilateral hilar lymphadenopathy as the sole finding
Large pleural effusion as the dominant feature
Uniform 1–3 mm nodules throughout both lungs
originalOptions: Ipsilateral hilar lymphadenopathy as the sole finding
Large pleural effusion as the dominant feature
Uniform 1–3 mm nodules throughout both lungs
questions.correctAnswer: B) Cavitation in the upper lobes
questions.explanation: Post-primary TB favors the upper zones and is far more likely to cavitate than primary TB. Isolated hilar nodes and effusion are features of primary disease, and diffuse tiny uniform nodules are miliary TB.

questions.text: What is the most important radiographic landmark of pneumothorax?
options: Increased density of the affected lung
Mediastinal shift toward the affected side
Air bronchograms within a homogeneous opacity
A visible visceral pleural edge with no lung markings peripheral to it
originalOptions: Increased density of the affected lung
Mediastinal shift toward the affected side
Air bronchograms within a homogeneous opacity
A visible visceral pleural edge with no lung markings peripheral to it
questions.correctAnswer: E) A visible visceral pleural edge with no lung markings peripheral to it
questions.correctAnswerText: A visible visceral pleural edge with no lung markings peripheral to it
questions.explanation: The thin white visceral pleural line with an avascular lucent space beyond it is the key sign. Mediastinal shift occurs only in tension pneumothorax, and the mediastinum shifts away, not toward the affected side.

questions.text: Which CT finding characterizes pulmonary embolism?
options: Intimal flap with a double lumen
Fusiform dilatation of the ascending aorta >4 cm
Filling defect within a pulmonary artery
originalOptions: Intimal flap with a double lumen
Fusiform dilatation of the ascending aorta >4 cm
Filling defect within a pulmonary artery
questions.correctAnswer: C) Filling defect within a pulmonary artery
questions.correctAnswerText: Filling defect within a pulmonary artery
questions.explanation: An intraluminal filling defect in the pulmonary arteries on CTPA is the hallmark of PE. The other options describe aortic dissection, aortic aneurysm, sarcoidosis and bronchiectasis respectively.

questions.text: Which of the following is FALSE regarding this lesion? [img: Radiologymnonossifyingfibroma.png ]
options: Most common benign non-ossifying fibrous lesion of bone
originalOptions: Most common benign non-ossifying fibrous lesion of bone
questions.explanation: Non-ossifying fibroma is a benign fibrous cortical lesion with a sclerotic rim and NO periosteal reaction; a sunburst pattern implies an aggressive process (e.g., osteosarcoma), which contradicts the benign nature of NOF.
questions.note: عندما جاء السؤال لدفعة ايورتا كان مصحوب بصورة ، أما عندما جاء لدفعة ايريس فكان بدون صورة لكن كان بالسؤال : Non-ossifying fibroma

questions.text: Which of the following is FALSE regarding this shoulder finding? [img: Radiologymanteriorshoulderdislocation.png ]
options: Anterior shoulder dislocation is the most common type
Caused by forced abduction, external rotation, and extension
Humeral head is displaced superiorly and anteriorly
Can cause axillary artery or nerve injury
originalOptions: Anterior shoulder dislocation is the most common type
Caused by forced abduction, external rotation, and extension
Humeral head is displaced superiorly and anteriorly
Can cause axillary artery or nerve injury
questions.correctAnswer: C) Humeral head is displaced superiorly and anteriorly
questions.correctAnswerText: Humeral head is displaced superiorly and anteriorly
questions.explanation: In anterior shoulder dislocation, the humeral head is displaced anteriorly and inferiorly (medially), not superiorly, distinguishing it from luxatio erecta (inferior dislocation).

questions.text: What is FALSE about this fracture? [img: Radiologymbucklefracture.png ]
options: Bulging of the cortex from axial loading
Common in the distal radius metaphysis in children
originalOptions: Bulging of the cortex from axial loading
Common in the distal radius metaphysis in children
questions.correctAnswer: A) Complete fracture through the bone
questions.explanation: A buckle (torus) fracture is an incomplete fracture with cortical bulging from axial compression, so describing it as a complete fracture is false.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymgout.png ]
questions.explanation: Punched-out juxta-articular erosions with overhanging edges and preserved joint space/bone density in the feet are classic for gout.

questions.text: Which is WRONG about this avulsion fracture pairing?
options: Anterior superior iliac spine – adductor muscles
Anterior inferior iliac spine – rectus femoris
originalOptions: Anterior superior iliac spine – adductor muscles
Anterior inferior iliac spine – rectus femoris
questions.correctAnswer: B) Anterior superior iliac spine – adductor muscles
questions.correctAnswerText: Anterior superior iliac spine – adductor muscles
questions.explanation: The ASIS is the origin of sartorius (and tensor fasciae latae), not the adductor group; adductors attach at the symphysis pubis.

questions.text: What is the name of the part of the corpus callosum indicated by the number 5? [img: Radiologynanatomysplenium.png ]
questions.correctAnswer: C) Splenium of the corpus callosum
questions.explanation: The arrow (5) points to the posterior, bulbous portion of the corpus callosum — the splenium — distinct from the genu (anterior) and body (mid-portion).
questions.note: 1. Rostrum || 2. Genu || 3. Body || 4. Isthmus || 5. Splenium

questions.text: Identify the indicated neuroanatomical structure (Number 2). [img: Radiologynanatomyhippocampus.png ]
questions.explanation: The labeled structure lies posteroinferior to the amygdala within the medial temporal lobe — the hippocampus — distinct from the amygdala (anterosuperior) and uncus (anteromedial tip).
questions.note: 1. Amygdala || 2. Head of hippocampus

questions.text: The cerebellum's blood supply mainly originates from which of the following?
questions.explanation: The SCA and AICA (branches of the basilar artery) supply most of the cerebellum; only PICA arises from the distal vertebral artery.

questions.text: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis – select the correct statement.
options: Non-contrast MRI shows a hypointense filling defect
Non-contrast CT shows a hyperdense ("dense") sinus
Contrast-enhanced MRI shows the "empty delta" sign
Contrast-enhanced CT shows the "empty delta" sign
originalOptions: Non-contrast MRI shows a hypointense filling defect
Non-contrast CT shows a hyperdense ("dense") sinus
Contrast-enhanced MRI shows the "empty delta" sign
Contrast-enhanced CT shows the "empty delta" sign
questions.correctAnswer: E) Contrast-enhanced CT shows the "empty delta" sign
questions.correctAnswerText: Contrast-enhanced CT shows the "empty delta" sign
questions.explanation: The empty delta sign is a triangular filling defect surrounded by enhancing dura, classically seen on contrast-enhanced CT venography; non-contrast CT instead shows a hyperdense (not empty) thrombosed sinus.

questions.text: What is the name of this radiological sign? [img: Radiologyafootballsign.png ]
questions.explanation: A massive pneumoperitoneum outlines the entire abdominal cavity in an oval, football-like shape on a supine film, which is the football sign (seen especially in neonates/infants).

questions.text: Which is not a typical finding in acute cholecystitis on ultrasound?
questions.explanation: Acute cholecystitis classically shows a thickened (>3 mm), edematous gallbladder wall; a thin, normal wall argues against the diagnosis.

questions.text: Gallbladder stones may be seen on ultrasound as:
options: Hyperechoic foci with posterior acoustic shadowing
originalOptions: Hyperechoic foci with posterior acoustic shadowing
questions.correctAnswer: B) Hyperechoic foci with posterior acoustic shadowing
questions.correctAnswerText: Hyperechoic foci with posterior acoustic shadowing
questions.explanation: Gallstones reflect sound strongly (hyperechoic) and block further transmission, producing a characteristic posterior acoustic shadow.

questions.text: Which is the most important imaging criterion for pyloric stenosis?
options: Single pyloric muscle wall thickness > 3 mm
originalOptions: Single pyloric muscle wall thickness > 3 mm
questions.correctAnswer: C) Single pyloric muscle wall thickness > 3 mm
questions.correctAnswerText: Single pyloric muscle wall thickness > 3 mm
questions.explanation: A single muscular wall thickness greater than 3 mm on transverse ultrasound is the most accurate criterion for hypertrophic pyloric stenosis.

questions.text: Which of the following radiological signs can make the surest distinction between sigmoid volvulus as opposed to cecal volvulus?
options: Whirlpool sign of the twisted mesenteric vessels
Absent haustral markings throughout the entire colon
A mass in the lower abdomen (pelvis) pointing toward the right upper quadrant
Coffee bean sign with medial deviation of the dilated loop
Multiple air-fluid levels on an erect film
originalOptions: Whirlpool sign of the twisted mesenteric vessels
Absent haustral markings throughout the entire colon
A mass in the lower abdomen (pelvis) pointing toward the right upper quadrant
Coffee bean sign with medial deviation of the dilated loop
Multiple air-fluid levels on an erect film
questions.correctAnswer: C) A mass in the lower abdomen (pelvis) pointing toward the right upper quadrant
questions.correctAnswerText: A mass in the lower abdomen (pelvis) pointing toward the right upper quadrant
questions.explanation: Sigmoid volvulus arises in the pelvis/left lower quadrant and its dilated loop characteristically points toward the RUQ, whereas cecal volvulus arises in the RLQ and points toward the epigastrium/LUQ — this site-of-origin-and-direction pattern is more reliable than haustral pattern or the whirlpool sign, both of which can overlap between volvulus types.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycpneumothorax.png ]
questions.explanation: Right-sided pneumothorax with almost complete collapse of the right lung. Mediastinal shift to the left, splayed right ribs and mild right diaphragm depression indicate increased right pleural pressure. A thin visceral pleural line with no lung markings peripheral to it and a lucent pleural space is diagnostic of pneumothorax. Effusion and consolidation produce opacity instead.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycconsolidationct.png ]
questions.explanation: Air-space opacification with air bronchograms and preserved lung volume is consolidation. Atelectasis shows volume loss, and effusion shows a meniscus without air bronchograms.

questions.text: What is the best imaging modality for diagnosing acute pulmonary embolism, for example in a patient with acute hypoxia and dyspnea with a normal chest X-ray?
questions.explanation: CTPA (which utilizes intravenous contrast) directly shows filling defects in the pulmonary arteries, and the chest X-ray is often normal. V/Q scan is only an alternative when contrast is contraindicated.

questions.text: What is the minimum volume of pleural fluid required to be visualized on a standard PA chest radiograph?
questions.explanation: About 250–600 mL is needed to detect an effusion on an erect PA film. Smaller volumes require lateral decubitus views or ultrasound.

questions.text: Stage II sarcoidosis is characterized by:
options: Hilar or mediastinal nodal enlargement only
originalOptions: Hilar or mediastinal nodal enlargement only
questions.correctAnswer: D) Nodal enlargement with parenchymal disease
questions.explanation: Stage II combines nodal enlargement with parenchymal disease. Stage I is nodal only, and stage III is parenchymal disease only.

questions.text: What is the most common location for cavitation in post-primary tuberculosis?
options: Anterior segments of the upper lobes
Posterior segments of the upper lobes
Basal segments of the lower lobes
originalOptions: Anterior segments of the upper lobes
Posterior segments of the upper lobes
Basal segments of the lower lobes
questions.correctAnswer: B) Posterior segments of the upper lobes
questions.correctAnswerText: Posterior segments of the upper lobes
questions.explanation: Post-primary TB develops mainly in the posterior segments of the upper lobes (~85%) and the superior segment of the lower lobe. The other locations are not typical.

questions.text: What is the structure injured in this image? [img: Radiologymquadricepstendon.png ]
questions.explanation: The lesion is at the tendon superior to the patella (quadriceps insertion), consistent with a ruptured quadriceps tendon; the PCL and meniscus are intra-articular structures not visualized in this location.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymosteochondroma.png ]
questions.explanation: A bony projection with cortical and medullary continuity with the parent bone, arising from the metaphysis and pointing away from the joint, is characteristic of osteochondroma (cartilage-capped exostosis).

questions.text: 'Rugger jersey spine' is seen in:
questions.explanation: Alternating dense-lucent-dense vertebral endplates (rugger jersey spine) are a classic radiographic sign of hyperparathyroidism.

questions.text: What is the most common location of osteoid osteoma?
questions.explanation: Long bones of the limb, especially the femoral neck, are the most common site for osteoid osteoma.

questions.text: Which of the following is a common Salter-Harris type 1 fracture?
questions.explanation: SCFE represents a Salter-Harris type I injury (slipped physis) through the proximal femoral growth plate.

questions.text: Which MRI sequence is shown in this image, where CSF is suppressed (dark) while periventricular lesions remain bright? [img: Radiologynflairsequence.png ]
questions.explanation: FLAIR nulls the CSF signal while preserving T2 hyperintensity of white matter lesions, unlike standard T2 (CSF bright) or T1 (different grey/white contrast).

questions.text: Which of the following is a cause of non-communicating hydrocephalus?
questions.explanation: A colloid cyst at the foramen of Monro physically obstructs CSF flow (non-communicating hydrocephalus); SAH, meningitis, and meningeal carcinomatosis impair CSF absorption (communicating), and choroid plexus papilloma causes communicating hydrocephalus via CSF overproduction.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about multiple sclerosis is FALSE?
options: CT is a better imaging tool than MRI for diagnosis
The McDonald criteria are used for diagnosis
MRI is the primary imaging modality for MS
originalOptions: CT is a better imaging tool than MRI for diagnosis
The McDonald criteria are used for diagnosis
MRI is the primary imaging modality for MS
questions.correctAnswer: B) CT is a better imaging tool than MRI for diagnosis
questions.correctAnswerText: CT is a better imaging tool than MRI for diagnosis
questions.explanation: MRI, not CT, is the modality of choice for MS since CT is often normal or nonspecific even with significant disease burden.

questions.text: Which artery supplies the infarcted territory shown in this image? [img: Radiologynacainfarct.png ]
questions.explanation: The infarct involves the medial frontal lobe, the classic ACA distribution, unlike the lateral hemispheric MCA territory or the occipital PCA territory.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynepiduralhematomaacute.png ]
questions.explanation: A biconvex, lentiform hyperdense extra-axial collection is the classic CT appearance of acute epidural hematoma, distinct from the crescentic shape of subdural hematoma.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaportalvenousgas.png ]
questions.explanation: The tiny branching gas foci extend to the peripheral 2 cm of the liver, characteristic of portal venous gas; pneumobilia by contrast is centrally distributed near the porta hepatis.

questions.text: Which statement is FALSE regarding hypertrophic pyloric stenosis?
options: Pyloric muscle thickness is typically > 3 mm
Pyloric canal length is usually > 15–18 mm
It commonly presents with non-bilious projectile vomiting
originalOptions: Pyloric muscle thickness is typically > 3 mm
Pyloric canal length is usually > 15–18 mm
It commonly presents with non-bilious projectile vomiting
questions.correctAnswer: D) Pyloric muscle thickness is < 7 mm
questions.explanation: There is no established "<7 mm" criterion for pyloric stenosis; the recognized diagnostic thickness threshold is greater than 3 mm, making this statement inaccurate and false.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a direct branch of the abdominal aorta?
questions.explanation: The splenic artery is a branch of the celiac trunk, not a direct branch of the abdominal aorta itself.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologycaorticdissection.png ]
questions.explanation: Contrast CT shows an intimal flap separating a true and a false lumen. An aneurysm is a fusiform dilatation without a flap, and pulmonary embolism gives filling defects in the pulmonary arteries.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about sarcoidosis staging is WRONG?
options: Stage I: hilar or mediastinal nodal enlargement only
Stage II: nodal enlargement with parenchymal disease
Stage IV: end-stage lung disease (pulmonary fibrosis)
originalOptions: Stage I: hilar or mediastinal nodal enlargement only
Stage II: nodal enlargement with parenchymal disease
Stage IV: end-stage lung disease (pulmonary fibrosis)
questions.correctAnswer: E) Stage II: parenchymal disease only
questions.explanation: Parenchymal disease without nodal enlargement is stage III. Stage II requires both nodal enlargement and parenchymal disease.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding pneumothorax is FALSE?
options: Primary spontaneous pneumothorax occurs without underlying lung disease
Emphysema is a cause of secondary spontaneous pneumothorax
Marfan syndrome is not associated with pneumothorax
The lateral decubitus film should be taken with the suspected side up
Mediastinal shift away from the pneumothorax occurs only in tension pneumothorax
originalOptions: Primary spontaneous pneumothorax occurs without underlying lung disease
Emphysema is a cause of secondary spontaneous pneumothorax
Marfan syndrome is not associated with pneumothorax
The lateral decubitus film should be taken with the suspected side up
Mediastinal shift away from the pneumothorax occurs only in tension pneumothorax
questions.correctAnswer: C) Marfan syndrome is not associated with pneumothorax
questions.correctAnswerText: Marfan syndrome is not associated with pneumothorax
questions.explanation: Marfan syndrome is a recognized cause of primary spontaneous pneumothorax, along with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency and homocystinuria. The other statements are correct.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about tuberculosis is FALSE?
options: Primary TB is more common in adults than in children
Cavitation is uncommon in primary TB
Post-primary TB has a strong upper-zone predilection
Post-primary TB is more likely to cavitate than primary TB
Ipsilateral hilar lymphadenopathy is more frequent in childhood primary TB
originalOptions: Primary TB is more common in adults than in children
Cavitation is uncommon in primary TB
Post-primary TB has a strong upper-zone predilection
Post-primary TB is more likely to cavitate than primary TB
Ipsilateral hilar lymphadenopathy is more frequent in childhood primary TB
questions.correctAnswer: A) Primary TB is more common in adults than in children
questions.correctAnswerText: Primary TB is more common in adults than in children
questions.explanation: Primary TB is more typical of children, with hilar nodes in about 90% of children versus 10–30% of adults. Adults mostly present with post-primary reactivation disease.

questions.text: What is the structure injured in this image? [img: Radiologymquadricepstendon.png ]
questions.explanation: The lesion is at the tendon superior to the patella (quadriceps insertion), consistent with a ruptured quadriceps tendon; the PCL and meniscus are intra-articular structures not visualized in this location.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologymosteochondroma.png ]
questions.explanation: A bony projection with cortical and medullary continuity with the parent bone, arising from the metaphysis and pointing away from the joint, is characteristic of osteochondroma (cartilage-capped exostosis).

questions.text: 'Rugger jersey spine' is seen in:
questions.explanation: Alternating dense-lucent-dense vertebral endplates (rugger jersey spine) are a classic radiographic sign of hyperparathyroidism.

questions.text: What is the most common location of osteoid osteoma?
questions.explanation: Long bones of the limb, especially the femoral neck, are the most common site for osteoid osteoma.

questions.text: Which of the following is a common Salter-Harris type 1 fracture?
questions.explanation: SCFE represents a Salter-Harris type I injury (slipped physis) through the proximal femoral growth plate.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologynepiduralhematomaacute.png ]
questions.explanation: A biconvex, lentiform hyperdense extra-axial collection is the classic CT appearance of acute epidural hematoma, distinct from the crescentic shape of subdural hematoma.

questions.text: Homogeneous enhancement and hyperdensity on non-contrast CT is most typical of which lesion?
questions.explanation: Primary CNS lymphoma is classically hyperdense on non-contrast CT (high cellularity) with homogeneous enhancement, unlike metastases or abscesses, which typically show ring enhancement with central necrosis.

questions.text: Which MRI sequence is most sensitive for detecting blood breakdown products (hemosiderin/deoxyhemoglobin)?
questions.explanation: Gradient echo/susceptibility-weighted sequences are exquisitely sensitive to blood products due to a blooming artifact, unlike T1, T2, or FLAIR.

questions.text: Which of the following is false regarding cecal volvulus?
options: Colonic haustral pattern is generally maintained
Extends towards the right upper quadrant
One air-fluid level may be seen
Distal colon is usually collapsed and the small bowel is distended
Arises in the right lower quadrant
originalOptions: Colonic haustral pattern is generally maintained
Extends towards the right upper quadrant
One air-fluid level may be seen
Distal colon is usually collapsed and the small bowel is distended
Arises in the right lower quadrant
questions.correctAnswer: B) Extends towards the right upper quadrant
questions.correctAnswerText: Extends towards the right upper quadrant
questions.explanation: Cecal volvulus classically extends toward the epigastrium or left upper quadrant, not the right upper quadrant, distinguishing it from the expected distension pattern.

questions.text: Which of the following is false regarding achalasia?
options: Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea
originalOptions: Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea
questions.explanation: Achalasia produces marked esophageal dilatation, not a normal-caliber esophagus, making this the false statement.

questions.text: Which of the following is true regarding acute cholecystitis?
options: Seen on ultrasound as hyperechoic foci with acoustic shadowing
originalOptions: Seen on ultrasound as hyperechoic foci with acoustic shadowing
questions.correctAnswer: D) Seen on ultrasound as hyperechoic foci with acoustic shadowing
questions.correctAnswerText: Seen on ultrasound as hyperechoic foci with acoustic shadowing
questions.explanation: Gallstones are hyperechoic with posterior shadowing on ultrasound; stones are actually hypointense (dark) on MRI, and cholecystitis typically shows gallbladder distension with pericholecystic edema, making the other options false.

questions.text: Which of the following appears radiolucent (translucent) on chest radiograph?
questions.explanation: Air in the pleural space is black (lucent). Effusion, consolidation, collapse and enlarged nodes are all soft-tissue opacities.

questions.text: All of the following are true about consolidation EXCEPT:
options: It can be caused by bronchoalveolar carcinoma
Volume loss of the affected lung
It may present as lobar or bronchopneumonia
originalOptions: It can be caused by bronchoalveolar carcinoma
Volume loss of the affected lung
It may present as lobar or bronchopneumonia
questions.correctAnswer: B) Volume loss of the affected lung
questions.correctAnswerText: Volume loss of the affected lung
questions.explanation: In consolidation, air is replaced by fluid, pus or cells, so lung volume is preserved. Volume loss indicates collapse.

questions.text: All of the following can cause lobar collapse EXCEPT:
options: Bullous emphysema of the involved lobe
originalOptions: Bullous emphysema of the involved lobe
questions.correctAnswer: E) Bullous emphysema of the involved lobe
questions.correctAnswerText: Bullous emphysema of the involved lobe
questions.explanation: Lobar collapse results from luminal obstruction (foreign body, mucus plug), mural lesions (carcinoma) or extrinsic compression. Bullous emphysema does not obstruct the supplying bronchus.

questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE about Pediatric MSK?
options: Osteogenesis imperfecta is a collagen type II disease
Rachitic rosary occurs at the posterior rib end
In SCFE the femoral head slips anteriorly and laterally
DDH shows a shallow acetabulum with cephalic subluxation or dislocation of the femoral head
In Perthes disease the femoral head is small and lucent
originalOptions: Osteogenesis imperfecta is a collagen type II disease
Rachitic rosary occurs at the posterior rib end
In SCFE the femoral head slips anteriorly and laterally
DDH shows a shallow acetabulum with cephalic subluxation or dislocation of the femoral head
In Perthes disease the femoral head is small and lucent
questions.correctAnswer: D) DDH shows a shallow acetabulum with cephalic subluxation or dislocation of the femoral head
questions.correctAnswerText: DDH shows a shallow acetabulum with cephalic subluxation or dislocation of the femoral head
questions.explanation: This accurately describes the acetabular dysplasia and superior femoral head displacement seen in DDH; OI is actually a type I collagen defect, and in Perthes the femoral head is sclerotic (not lucent).

questions.text: What is the most common type of Salter-Harris fracture?
questions.explanation: Salter-Harris type II accounts for approximately 75% of physeal fractures, making it by far the most common subtype.

questions.text: Which of the following does NOT occur in the metaphysis in a skeletally mature individual?
questions.explanation: Giant cell tumor of bone classically occurs in the epiphysis extending to the subchondral bone in skeletally mature patients, unlike the other listed metaphyseal lesions.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT seen in ankylosing spondylitis?
questions.explanation: Ankylosing spondylitis produces enthesophytes, syndesmophytes, ligament ossification, and dural ectasia; spinal canal stenosis is not a classic direct radiologic feature of this disease.

questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE about arthritis?
options: In septic arthritis, post-contrast fat-saturated T1 shows synovial thickening
Syndesmophytes run perpendicular to the spine
In osteoarthritis, sclerosis occurs with severe osteopenia
In rheumatoid arthritis, marginal erosions occur at the medial aspect of the MCP joints
Joint space and bone density are normal in septic arthritis
originalOptions: In septic arthritis, post-contrast fat-saturated T1 shows synovial thickening
Syndesmophytes run perpendicular to the spine
In osteoarthritis, sclerosis occurs with severe osteopenia
In rheumatoid arthritis, marginal erosions occur at the medial aspect of the MCP joints
Joint space and bone density are normal in septic arthritis
questions.correctAnswer: A) In septic arthritis, post-contrast fat-saturated T1 shows synovial thickening
questions.correctAnswerText: In septic arthritis, post-contrast fat-saturated T1 shows synovial thickening
questions.explanation: MRI in septic arthritis shows synovial thickening on post-contrast fat-saturated T1; syndesmophytes actually run parallel (not perpendicular) to the spine, and RA erosions occur at the radial (not medial) MCP aspect.

questions.text: Regarding avulsion fractures, which of the following is TRUE?
questions.explanation: The adductor muscle group originates from the pubic symphysis/pubic rami, making this the correct pairing; hamstrings actually attach at the ischial tuberosity and rectus femoris at the AIIS.

questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE about aneurysmal bone cyst?
options: Metaphyseal location with multiple fluid-fluid level cysts
Solid periosteal reaction is always present
Occurs almost exclusively in elderly patients
originalOptions: Metaphyseal location with multiple fluid-fluid level cysts
Solid periosteal reaction is always present
Occurs almost exclusively in elderly patients
questions.correctAnswer: B) Metaphyseal location with multiple fluid-fluid level cysts
questions.correctAnswerText: Metaphyseal location with multiple fluid-fluid level cysts
questions.explanation: ABC is an eccentric expansile metaphyseal lesion showing multiple blood-filled cystic spaces with fluid-fluid levels from layering blood products of different ages.

questions.text: All of the following can present in neurofibromatosis type 2, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Multiple cutaneous/subcutaneous neurofibromas are a hallmark of NF1, not NF2; NF2 instead features bilateral vestibular schwannomas, meningiomas, and intramedullary ependymomas.

questions.text: Which of the following is a white matter structure?
questions.explanation: The corona radiata is composed of white matter projection fibers; the others are all grey matter structures.

questions.text: All of the following are true about schizencephaly, EXCEPT:
options: It is a white matter-lined cleft extending from the ependyma to the pia mater
It can be unilateral or bilateral
Open-lip schizencephaly presents with more symptoms than closed-lip
There is pial communication in closed-lip schizencephaly
originalOptions: It is a white matter-lined cleft extending from the ependyma to the pia mater
It can be unilateral or bilateral
Open-lip schizencephaly presents with more symptoms than closed-lip
There is pial communication in closed-lip schizencephaly
questions.correctAnswer: A) It is a white matter-lined cleft extending from the ependyma to the pia mater
questions.correctAnswerText: It is a white matter-lined cleft extending from the ependyma to the pia mater
questions.explanation: Schizencephaly clefts are actually lined by grey matter (heterotopic cortex), not white matter. Laterality, symptom severity, and the presence of pial-ependymal communication in both types are all accurate characteristics of the condition.
questions.note: This question is not covered in the course slides.

questions.text: All of the following are intramedullary lesions, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Schwannoma is an intradural extramedullary tumor arising from a nerve root sheath, unlike astrocytoma, ependymoma, hemangioblastoma, and ganglioglioma, which are intramedullary.

questions.text: All of the following appear hyperintense on T2 MRI, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Air produces a signal void and appears hypointense on all MRI sequences, unlike fatty marrow, late subacute hematoma, choroid plexus papilloma, and GBM, which are typically T2 hyperintense.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT found in hyperacute brain ischemia?
options: Loss of the insular ribbon sign
Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
originalOptions: Loss of the insular ribbon sign
Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
questions.correctAnswer: E) Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
questions.correctAnswerText: Gliosis, volume loss, and cortical calcification
questions.explanation: These are late/chronic infarct changes (>3 weeks); the hyperacute stage (0–6 hours) instead shows subtle grey-white loss, cortical hypodensity, gyral effacement, and loss of the insular ribbon sign.

questions.text: Which of the following sutures joins the parietal bones with the occipital bone?
questions.explanation: The lambdoid suture joins both parietal bones with the occipital bone posteriorly; coronal joins frontal to parietal, sagittal joins the two parietals, and metopic joins the two frontal bones.

questions.text: Which of the following sutures joins the frontal and parietal bones?
questions.explanation: The coronal suture joins the frontal and parietal bones, distinct from the squamosal suture which joins the temporal and parietal bones, the metopic suture which joins the two frontal bones, the sagittal suture which joins the two parietal bones, and the lambdoid suture which joins the occipital and parietal bones.

questions.text: Regarding abdominal calcifications, which one of the following is TRUE?
options: Phleboliths are small arterial wall calcifications seen in the pelvis
Bilateral adrenal calcifications seen at the level of L5 usually
Eighty five percent of gall bladder stones seen on CT Scan
Eighty five percent of renal stones seen on Radiograph
The most likely diagnosis of pelvic calcification in a male is intravesical stone
originalOptions: Phleboliths are small arterial wall calcifications seen in the pelvis
Bilateral adrenal calcifications seen at the level of L5 usually
Eighty five percent of gall bladder stones seen on CT Scan
Eighty five percent of renal stones seen on Radiograph
The most likely diagnosis of pelvic calcification in a male is intravesical stone
questions.correctAnswer: D) Eighty five percent of renal stones seen on Radiograph
questions.correctAnswerText: Eighty five percent of renal stones seen on Radiograph
questions.explanation: Approximately 85% of urinary/renal stones are radio-opaque and visible on plain radiograph (X-ray); phleboliths are small venous (not arterial) calcifications, and adrenal glands lie much higher than L5.

questions.text: Regarding Free air in the abdomen, which of following is TRUE?
options: History of abdominal surgery within one month is an indication of pneumoperitoneum
The most common cause of free intraperitoneal air is perforated sigmoid colon
Falciform ligament sign lowers the possibility of pneumoperitoneum
Portal venous gas is only seen in the center of the liver
Erect chest radiograph is more sensitive to detect pneumoperitoneum compared to supine abdominal radiograph
originalOptions: History of abdominal surgery within one month is an indication of pneumoperitoneum
The most common cause of free intraperitoneal air is perforated sigmoid colon
Falciform ligament sign lowers the possibility of pneumoperitoneum
Portal venous gas is only seen in the center of the liver
Erect chest radiograph is more sensitive to detect pneumoperitoneum compared to supine abdominal radiograph
questions.correctAnswer: E) Erect chest radiograph is more sensitive to detect pneumoperitoneum compared to supine abdominal radiograph
questions.correctAnswerText: Erect chest radiograph is more sensitive to detect pneumoperitoneum compared to supine abdominal radiograph
questions.explanation: An erect chest film is the most sensitive plain radiograph for detecting free subdiaphragmatic gas; the falciform ligament sign actually supports (not lowers) the diagnosis, and portal venous gas is peripheral, not central.

questions.text: Regarding bowel obstruction, which of the following is TRUE?
options: Ascending colon diameter of 8 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Hernia is the most common cause of small bowel obstruction
Cecal diameter of 7 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Sigmoid volvulus usually extends to the left upper quadrant
Two air fluid levels of 3 cm width each apply the definition of obstruction
originalOptions: Ascending colon diameter of 8 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Hernia is the most common cause of small bowel obstruction
Cecal diameter of 7 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
Sigmoid volvulus usually extends to the left upper quadrant
Two air fluid levels of 3 cm width each apply the definition of obstruction
questions.correctAnswer: A) Ascending colon diameter of 8 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
questions.correctAnswerText: Ascending colon diameter of 8 cm meets the criteria of dilatation
questions.explanation: The "3-6-9 rule" sets the large bowel dilatation threshold at 6 cm, so 8 cm exceeds this; the cecal threshold is actually 9 cm, and adhesions (not hernia) are the overall most common cause of small bowel obstruction.

questions.text: Regarding abdomen anatomy, which of the following is TRUE?
options: The portal vein confluence lies anterior to the neck of the pancreas
The left adrenal gland lies more superiorly (cephalad) than the right adrenal gland
The right renal vein is longer than the left renal vein
The third part of the duodenum passes between liver and pancreas
The Inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L3
originalOptions: The portal vein confluence lies anterior to the neck of the pancreas
The left adrenal gland lies more superiorly (cephalad) than the right adrenal gland
The right renal vein is longer than the left renal vein
The third part of the duodenum passes between liver and pancreas
The Inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L3
questions.correctAnswer: E) The Inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L3
questions.correctAnswerText: The Inferior mesenteric artery arises at the level of L3
questions.explanation: The IMA arises from the anterior aorta at L3; the portal vein actually forms posterior (not anterior) to the pancreatic neck, the right (not left) adrenal gland sits more cephalad, and the left (not right) renal vein is the longer vessel.

questions.text: All of the following can cause lobar collapse EXCEPT:
options: Bullous emphysema of the involved lobe
originalOptions: Bullous emphysema of the involved lobe
questions.correctAnswer: E) Bullous emphysema of the involved lobe
questions.correctAnswerText: Bullous emphysema of the involved lobe
questions.explanation: Lobar collapse results from luminal obstruction (foreign body, mucus plug), mural lesions (carcinoma) or extrinsic compression. Bullous emphysema does not obstruct the supplying bronchus.

questions.text: An infant is suspected of having left-sided foreign body aspiration. Which of the following chest views is NOT helpful?
questions.explanation: With a check-valve obstruction, the affected lung fails to deflate on expiration or when the affected side is dependent (left lateral decubitus). A right lateral decubitus view gives no additional information for a left-sided foreign body.

questions.text: Regarding the pathology seen on the provided image, which of the following is TRUE? [img: Radiologyclobarconsolidation.png ]
options: Mediastinal shift to the same side aids the diagnosis of consolidation
The presence of air bronchograms aids the diagnosis of collapse
Lobar consolidation is usually bordered by a lung fissure
Clear outline of adjacent structures aids the diagnosis of pleural fluid
Volume loss of the affected lobe is the hallmark of consolidation
originalOptions: Mediastinal shift to the same side aids the diagnosis of consolidation
The presence of air bronchograms aids the diagnosis of collapse
Lobar consolidation is usually bordered by a lung fissure
Clear outline of adjacent structures aids the diagnosis of pleural fluid
Volume loss of the affected lobe is the hallmark of consolidation
questions.correctAnswer: C) Lobar consolidation is usually bordered by a lung fissure
questions.correctAnswerText: Lobar consolidation is usually bordered by a lung fissure
questions.explanation: Lobar consolidation is sharply demarcated by the fissure. Shift toward the lesion and volume loss suggest collapse, and effusion obscures adjacent structures.

questions.text: Regarding the provided image, what is the best management for the pathology seen? [img: Radiologycpneumoniamanagement.png ]
questions.explanation: The image shows consolidation from bacterial pneumonia, which is treated with antibiotics. A chest tube is for pneumothorax or empyema, and diuretics are for pulmonary edema in heart failure.

questions.text: Regarding pneumothorax, which of the following is TRUE?
options: Mediastinal shift to the left is usually associated with left tension pneumothorax
Cavitary neoplasms are the usual cause of primary pneumothorax
The chest tube should be inserted anterosuperiorly at the affected side
Primary spontaneous pneumothorax typically occurs in short elderly women
originalOptions: Mediastinal shift to the left is usually associated with left tension pneumothorax
Cavitary neoplasms are the usual cause of primary pneumothorax
The chest tube should be inserted anterosuperiorly at the affected side
Primary spontaneous pneumothorax typically occurs in short elderly women
questions.correctAnswer: D) The chest tube should be inserted anterosuperiorly at the affected side
questions.correctAnswerText: The chest tube should be inserted anterosuperiorly at the affected side
questions.explanation: Air collects anteriorly and superiorly, so the tube is placed there. Laceration causes an ipsilateral pneumothorax, tension pushes the mediastinum away, and primary spontaneous pneumothorax affects tall young patients.

questions.text: The demonstration of an abnormal fat pad in an adult suggests which of the following?
questions.explanation: The most common cause of an elbow fat pad sign (joint effusion) in adults is a radial head fracture, whereas supracondylar fracture is the classic pediatric cause.

questions.text: What is the most common type of Salter-Harris fracture?
questions.explanation: Salter-Harris type II accounts for approximately 75% of physeal fractures, making it by far the most common subtype.

questions.text: Punched-out erosion with sclerotic margins is a typical radiological finding in which of the following?
questions.explanation: Well-defined "punched-out" erosions with sclerotic, overhanging margins are pathognomonic for gout, unlike the ill-defined marginal erosions of RA.

questions.text: Regarding non-accidental trauma, which of the following is TRUE?
options: Epiphyseal corner fracture is highly specific for child abuse
Extradural hematoma is one of the most common brain findings
Infants are at greatest risk of abuse
Anterior rib fracture is highly specific for child abuse
Skeletal survey is not recommended in cases of suspected child abuse
originalOptions: Epiphyseal corner fracture is highly specific for child abuse
Extradural hematoma is one of the most common brain findings
Infants are at greatest risk of abuse
Anterior rib fracture is highly specific for child abuse
Skeletal survey is not recommended in cases of suspected child abuse
questions.correctAnswer: C) Infants are at greatest risk of abuse
questions.correctAnswerText: Infants are at greatest risk of abuse
questions.explanation: Non-ambulatory infants are at highest risk of NAI; note that it is the metaphyseal (not epiphyseal) corner fracture and posterior (not anterior) rib fractures that are highly specific.

questions.text: Regarding ankylosing spondylitis, which of the following is FALSE?
options: Sacroiliitis is a late radiological manifestation
It is a disease of young adults
Interspinous ligament ossification gives a "dagger spine" appearance
originalOptions: Sacroiliitis is a late radiological manifestation
It is a disease of young adults
Interspinous ligament ossification gives a "dagger spine" appearance
questions.correctAnswer: A) Sacroiliitis is a late radiological manifestation
questions.correctAnswerText: Sacroiliitis is a late radiological manifestation
questions.explanation: Sacroiliitis is typically the FIRST radiological manifestation of ankylosing spondylitis, not a late one.

questions.text: Which of the following is the earliest radiological finding in rheumatoid arthritis?
questions.explanation: Fusiform periarticular soft tissue swelling (from effusion/tenosynovitis) can be the earliest or only radiographic finding in RA, preceding visible marginal erosions.

questions.text: Regarding osteosarcoma, which of the following is FALSE?
options: Primary osteosarcoma typically occurs in young patients
Secondary osteosarcoma occurs in the elderly
Commonly associated with an aggressive periosteal reaction
originalOptions: Primary osteosarcoma typically occurs in young patients
Secondary osteosarcoma occurs in the elderly
Commonly associated with an aggressive periosteal reaction
questions.correctAnswer: B) Typically occurs in the epiphysis
questions.explanation: Osteosarcoma most commonly arises in the metadiaphysis/metaphysis around the knee, not the epiphysis, making this statement false.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a recognized cause of diffuse cerebral edema? [img: Radiologyndiffuseedema.png ]
questions.explanation: Migraine is not a cause of diffuse cerebral edema; drug overdose, hypertensive emergency (PRES), anoxic injury, and trauma are all recognized causes of diffuse brain swelling.

questions.text: Which of the following is a cause of non-communicating hydrocephalus?
questions.explanation: A colloid cyst at the foramen of Monro physically obstructs CSF flow (non-communicating hydrocephalus); SAH, meningitis, and meningeal carcinomatosis impair CSF absorption (communicating), and choroid plexus papilloma causes communicating hydrocephalus via CSF overproduction.

questions.text: Which of the following sutures joins the two parietal bones?
questions.explanation: The sagittal suture runs in the midline joining the two parietal bones to each other.

questions.text: Regarding cerebral sinus thrombosis, which of the following is TRUE?
options: Sinus thrombosis is an occlusion of arterial channels in the cranial cavity
The empty delta sign is a common radiological finding on T1 MRI with contrast
The dura typically does not enhance
A hypodense sinus is seen on non-contrast CT
originalOptions: Sinus thrombosis is an occlusion of arterial channels in the cranial cavity
The empty delta sign is a common radiological finding on T1 MRI with contrast
The dura typically does not enhance
A hypodense sinus is seen on non-contrast CT
questions.correctAnswer: C) The empty delta sign is a common radiological finding on T1 MRI with contrast
questions.correctAnswerText: The empty delta sign is a common radiological finding on T1 MRI with contrast
questions.explanation: The empty delta sign — a triangular filling defect surrounded by enhancing dura — is classically seen on contrast-enhanced imaging; sinus thrombosis is a venous (not arterial) occlusion, acute thrombus typically does NOT enhance, the dura DOES enhance, and non-contrast CT shows a hyperdense (not hypodense) sinus.

questions.text: Regarding subdural hematoma, which of the following is TRUE?
options: It does not cross the falx cerebri
It is usually caused by a tear in the middle meningeal artery
It forms between the inner skull table and the outer dural layer
originalOptions: It does not cross the falx cerebri
It is usually caused by a tear in the middle meningeal artery
It forms between the inner skull table and the outer dural layer
questions.correctAnswer: A) It does not cross the falx cerebri
questions.correctAnswerText: It does not cross the falx cerebri
questions.explanation: Subdural hematoma is confined by the falx cerebri and tentorium but CAN cross suture lines (opposite epidural hematoma); it is typically caused by bridging vein tears (not the middle meningeal artery) and has a crescentic (not lenticular) shape.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyapneumobilia.png ]
questions.explanation: The gas is centrally located within the biliary tree near the porta hepatis; portal venous gas classically extends to within 2 cm of the liver capsule (peripheral), which distinguishes it from pneumobilia.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyapneumoperitoneum.png ]
questions.explanation: Free intraperitoneal air is seen outlining the bowel loops and under the diaphragm, diagnostic of pneumoperitoneum rather than a fluid- or obstruction-related process.

questions.text: What is the diagnosis? [img: Radiologyahydronephrosis.png ]
questions.explanation: The coronal CT shows dilatation of the left renal collecting system (pelvicalyceal dilation) without a discrete simple fluid collection, consistent with hydronephrosis rather than an isolated stone or cyst.

questions.text: Not true about achalasia?
options: Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea is seen on the frontal view
originalOptions: Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea is seen on the frontal view
questions.correctAnswer: D) Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea is seen on the frontal view
questions.correctAnswerText: Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea is seen on the frontal view
questions.explanation: Anterior tracheal displacement/bowing from the dilated esophagus is a lateral-view finding, not a frontal-view finding, making this statement false.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaappendicitisus.jpg ]
questions.explanation: The imaging (Ultrasound) shows a dilated, non-compressible appendix with periappendiceal fluid/fat stranding ± appendicolith, the classic combination for acute appendicitis.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaleftrenalstone.png ]
questions.explanation: A well-defined, rounded radiopaque calcification overlying the renal shadow on KUB is most consistent with a renal calculus rather than a pelvic phlebolith or lymph node calcification.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaureterstone.png ]
questions.explanation: The calcification lies along the expected course of the ureter (from renal pelvis to bladder), distinguishing it from a phlebolith, which sits in the pelvis away from this line.

questions.text: Which imaging modality and plane is shown in this image? [img: Radiologyacoronalctabdomen.png ]
questions.correctAnswer: B) Coronal CT abdomen with contrast
questions.explanation: The image demonstrates the liver, kidneys, and spine in a coronal (frontal) cross-sectional plane typical of coronal reformatted contrast-enhanced CT.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyamidgutvolvulus.png ]
questions.explanation: The CT shows the classic whirlpool sign of the superior mesenteric vessels and mesentery twisting around each other, diagnostic of midgut volvulus (from malrotation).

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyagallstoneus.png ]
questions.explanation: Ultrasound shows a hyperechoic intraluminal focus with posterior acoustic shadowing within the gallbladder, the classic appearance of a gallstone.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyaachalasia.png ]
questions.explanation: The barium swallow shows a dilated esophagus tapering smoothly to a "bird-beak" narrowing at the gastroesophageal junction, the classic finding of achalasia.

questions.text: Which of the following is false regarding achalasia?
options: Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea
originalOptions: Anterior displacement and bowing of the trachea
questions.explanation: Achalasia produces marked esophageal dilatation, not a normal-caliber esophagus, making this the false statement.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis? [img: Radiologyagastriccancer.png ]
